newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-1995/96 record year for Australia winemakers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-1995/96 record year for Australia winemakers.

text.p: Australia's wine industry enjoyed a bumber year in the year to June 30 1996, with record production and exports, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.

Wine production jumped 32 percent to 606.1 million litres from 458.4 million litres in 1994/95 and was 14 percent higher than the previous record of 530.5 million litres in the year to end-June 1994, the bureau said.
The production data covers Australia's major wine producers, those which crush more than 400 tonnes of grapes.
Wine exports reached record levels in volume and value, the bureau said.

Export volumes reached 129.5 million litres in 1995/96, 14 percent higher than the 113.7 million litres the previous year and three percent higher than the previous record, 125.5 million litres in 1993/94.
The value of Australia's wine exports, mostly table wines, increased 22 percent to A$470.7 million from A$385.7 million in 1994/95, which was also the previous record.

The United Kingdom was the largest importer of Australian wine, taking 62.0 million litres, worth A$212.2 million, followed by the United States with 15.9 million litres ($79.5 million) and New Zealand (13.2 million litres, A$34.4 million).

Domestic sales of Australian produced wine continued their downward trend, falling 1.0 percent to 309.5 million litres from 313.4 million litres and 6.0 percent below the 1987/88 record of 330.5 million litres.
Wine imports, mostly table wines, also set a record for volume, but value was down.
Import volumes reached 20.3 million litres, compared with the previous record of 14.1 million litres in 1994/95. But the import value fell to A$60.5 million from the 1994/95 record of A$61.1 million.
